title: ChatGPT's new College Planner will help teens track applications, deadlines and financial aid
key_facts: OpenAI plans to add College Planner to ChatGPT for Teens, bringing application requirements, deadlines and financial-aid tasks into one plan for US four-year college applicants.
First version is for US high-school students in grades 10 to 12; described as coming soon with no release date.
OpenAI is supporting College Advising Corps, a nonprofit; the article says the funding amount and participating states were not specified.
New study tools: multi-page note capture into one PDF on iOS (Android in development), flashcards from notes or a topic, and interactive quizzes in chat.
OpenAI reports nearly 1.2 million teens used Learning Visualizations in one week and over 180,000 used Study Mode; the article says these figures show use, not measured learning gains.
OpenAI says teens spend under 15 minutes a day on ChatGPT on average; the article says the break-reminder figures do not show the reminder caused users to stop.
OpenAI committed three years of support to Boston Children's Hospital's Digital Wellness Lab and its student advisory council.
quote_evidence: OpenAI plans to add College Planner to ChatGPT for Teens, bringing application requirements, deadlines and financial-aid tasks into a single plan for students applying to US four-year colleges.
Those figures describe use of the tools, rather than measured improvements in learning.
why_it_matters_hint: Teens get an AI organiser for college applications, though it is not yet available and its benefits are unmeasured.
event_date: Announcement date not stated (article published 8 Oct 2026).
notes: Announcement is OpenAI's own (LinkedIn); the planner is not yet released; usage figures are OpenAI's.
